newsitem.title: UK: Dirty tanker chartering slow, rates mainly stable.
newsitem.headline: Dirty tanker chartering slow, rates mainly stable.

text.p: Dirty tanker chartering remaind slow in most regions on Tuesday, but traders said there was sufficient business on key routes and tonnage to underpin rates.

After softening in thinner trade on Monday, rates for VLCC tonnage in the Mideast Gulf for voyages East were holding steady as demand picked up. A vessel was booked Mideast Gulf to Japan at a slightly higher W56.5, up two points from Monday.

Brokers said weaker early Nov rates were caused by surplus older tonnage looking for trade. Mideast Gulf to Japan voyages were booked at W54.5 for early November on Monday but second and third decade November were holding around W57 today.
"Charterers have been able to take advantage of some very cheap rates, particularly for voyages to the Far East, a broker said.
Trade Mideast to Singapore and to the West was slow with 80,000 tonnes from Yanbu to the U.S. Alantic coast/Gulf traded around five points softer at W110.
Steady but quiet business out of West Africa saw rates soften a little on Monday but values were holding steady today despite the focus of trade staying mainly to the UK/Cont.

Suezmax tonnage was booked to the U.S. Gulf at W92.5 on Monday, off around five points from Friday but was holding the level today and a voyage from West Africa to Spain took a steady W102.5 amid good interest for million barrel tonnage for UK/Cont voyages.
Despite a steady flow of Suezmax business recently rates, particularly in the Med and UKC are expected to weaken further as more and more surplus tonnage becomes available.
Rates for Aframax tonnege in the Mediterranean and North Sea sectors have remained fairly stable with good cross-Med and Inter UK/Cont demand seen recently.
